strengths: The problem has an identifiable audience in code representation learning, reverse engineering, and software security. Learning representations from paired source code, LLVM IR, and generated summaries is a useful direction with potential applications across tasks.

Table VII provides promising evidence of transfer to x86 similarity search, particularly across substantially different optimization levels. For example, zero-shot COMBO improves O0/O3 MRR at pool size 1,000 from GraphCodeBERT’s 0.108 to 0.129. Reporting individual optimization pairs makes the uneven benefits visible.

The architecture diagrams, interpolation equations, and training schedules communicate the intended workflow reasonably well. Public datasets and detailed result tables provide a useful starting point for further investigation.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the evaluation protocol inconsistencies. Section IV-B and Table II specify disjoint POJ-104 training, validation, and test problem labels, yet Section V-B describes supervised classification into 104 classes and reports averages across all 104. Ordinary supervised classification cannot evaluate previously unseen class labels as described. Clarify whether this is classification, retrieval, or another protocol, and provide results under a valid held-out evaluation. The BinaryCorp statement that both training and test sets are used for fine-tuning also requires clarification; it leaves test isolation uncertain without establishing that leakage occurred.

Necessary: Align the claims with the actual input representations and prediction tasks. Pre-training and POJ-104 use LLVM IR generated from source, while Section V-D explicitly evaluates source-code vulnerability analysis. These experiments do not establish the claimed effectiveness on three executable-binary tasks. RQ4 also alternates between detecting vulnerable versus normal code and classifying already-vulnerable snippets into six categories. Specify the inputs, labels, negative examples, and splits, then narrow the binary-vulnerability claims or supply the corresponding binary evaluation.

Necessary: Provide evidence that isolates the proposed components. Table V compares sequential stages with additional training and different contrastive inputs and targets. Lower losses across those stages do not establish that interpolation improves representation quality. COMBO versus COMBO-Light likewise changes the training budget throughout. An equal-budget comparison against primary contrastive learning without interpolation, evaluated on downstream tasks, is needed to support the central component-effectiveness claim. Claims specifically attributing benefits to generated comments or the gradual schedule also need appropriate controls or narrower wording.

Necessary: Complete the method specification. The actual encoder architectures/checkpoints, tokenization and truncation, projection dimensions, and essential pre-training settings are insufficiently specified. Referencing SimpleCLIP does not resolve these choices for this architecture. Equation (4) also omits the softmax described in the prose before its targets enter cross-entropy. State the exact loss, normalization, temperature, gradient handling through targets, and representation used for binary-only inference. These details materially affect reproducibility and interpretation of the reported losses.

Necessary: Reconcile metric definitions and headline numbers. The claimed 5.45% average improvement lacks an explicit reference baseline and aggregation rule. In Table VIII, the reported MicroF1 matches the unweighted mean of the six displayed category F1 scores to rounding, while MacroF1 does not; explain the averaging units and computation. Table V also reports a 25.6% reduction from 0.048 to 0.039, whereas those values imply 18.75%. These discrepancies require checking the reported calculations.

Necessary: Calibrate comparative claims to the evidence. The experiments compare primarily against source-language models, despite discussing relevant binary methods such as jTrans. Either restrict superiority claims to the evaluated baselines or include an appropriate binary-specific comparison. Moreover, improvements such as 0.696 to 0.700 F1 in Table VI and 0.671 to 0.673 reported MacroF1 in Table VIII lack uncertainty estimates. Provide suitable variability estimates or temper claims of reliable superiority. Acceptance does not depend on achieving state-of-the-art performance.

Optional: Present the human gradual-learning analogy as motivation rather than an established explanation. Clarify that coordinate-wise mixing in Equation (11) need not lie on the line segment between the two embeddings. Additional compiler settings, architectures, and computational-cost measurements would broaden the paper’s usefulness.
